library.Adafruit_BMP280: Reads the BMP280 sensor: air temperature, air pressure and the altitude worked out from them.
library.Adafruit_BusIO: Helper classes that Adafruit drivers use to talk to chips over I2C and SPI and to read and write their registers.
library.Adafruit_GFX: Core graphics library: lines, shapes, bitmaps and text for many displays, including OLEDs.
library.Adafruit_MPU6050: Reads the MPU6050 motion sensor over I2C: 3-axis acceleration, 3-axis rotation speed and temperature.
library.Adafruit_NeoPixel: Controls addressable RGB LED strips and rings (WS2812, NeoPixel) from one data pin.
library.Adafruit_Sensor: Common sensor interface shared by Adafruit drivers, so every sensor reports readings the same way.
library.Adafruit_SSD1306: Drives small monochrome SSD1306 OLED screens (128x64 or 128x32) over I2C or SPI.
library.DallasTemperature: Reads DS18B20 and other Dallas/Maxim 1-Wire thermometers in °C or °F, using the OneWire library.
library.DHT: Reads temperature and humidity from DHT11, DHT22 and similar sensors on one digital pin.
library.EEPROM: Stores bytes that survive power-off in the 1024-byte EEPROM of the Uno.
library.Keypad: Reads matrix keypads such as 4x4 and 4x3 membrane keypads.
library.LiquidCrystal_I2C: Drives 16x2 and 20x4 character LCDs through an I2C backpack, using only the SDA and SCL pins.
library.NewPing: Measures distance with ultrasonic sensors like the HC-SR04, in centimetres or inches.
library.OneWire: Talks to 1-Wire devices such as the DS18B20 thermometer, many of which can share one data pin.
library.Servo: Drives hobby servo motors from any digital pin (up to 12 on the Uno).
library.SoftwareSerial: Adds extra serial ports on other digital pins, for modules like Bluetooth or GPS.
library.SPI: Fast serial link to devices like SD cards and displays, using pins 11 (MOSI), 12 (MISO) and 13 (SCK) on the Uno.
library.Stepper: Drives unipolar and bipolar stepper motors through a driver board, one step at a time.
library.VL53L0X: Pololu driver for the VL53L0X laser distance sensor, measuring up to about 2 m in millimetres over I2C.
library.Wire: Talks to I2C devices such as displays and sensors over two wires: SDA (A4) and SCL (A5) on the Uno.

setup.summary: Runs once when the board powers up or resets. Put pin modes and Serial.begin() here.

loop.summary: Runs again and again after setup() finishes, for as long as the board is powered.

serialEvent.summary: If you define it, it is called between loop() runs whenever new serial data has arrived.

pinMode.summary: Sets a pin to work as an input or an output. Call it in setup() before using the pin.

params.pin: Pin number (0 to 13, or A0 to A5 on the Uno).

digitalWrite.summary: Sets an output pin HIGH (5 V) or LOW (0 V). On an INPUT pin, HIGH turns on the internal pull-up.

digitalRead.summary: Reads whether a digital pin is HIGH or LOW.

analogRead.summary: Measures the voltage on an analog pin. 0 V gives 0 and 5 V gives 1023; one reading takes about 100 µs.

analogWrite.summary: Outputs a PWM signal to dim an LED or set a motor speed. Works on pins 3, 5, 6, 9, 10 and 11 of the Uno.

params.pin: A PWM pin (marked with ~ on the board).
params.value: Duty cycle from 0 (always off) to 255 (always on).

analogReference.summary: Chooses the voltage that analogRead() treats as its top value (1023).

params.mode: DEFAULT (5 V), INTERNAL (1.1 V) or EXTERNAL (voltage on the AREF pin).

delay.summary: Pauses the sketch. Nothing else in loop() runs while it waits.

params.ms: Time to wait in milliseconds (1000 = one second).

delayMicroseconds.summary: Pauses for a very short time. Accurate from about 3 µs up to 16383 µs.

millis.summary: Time since the board started. Use it to time things without blocking like delay() does.
millis.returns: Milliseconds since start; rolls over to 0 after about 50 days.

micros.summary: Time since the board started, in finer steps than millis().
micros.returns: Microseconds since start, in steps of 4 µs; rolls over after about 70 minutes.

yield.summary: Gives background tasks a chance to run. Called automatically while delay() waits; rarely needed in sketches.

pulseIn.summary: Waits for a pulse on a pin and measures how long it lasts, for example the echo of an ultrasonic sensor.

params.state: HIGH to time a high pulse, LOW to time a low pulse.
params.timeout: Longest time to wait in microseconds (default 1000000, one second).

pulseIn.returns: Pulse length in microseconds, or 0 if no pulse came before the timeout.

pulseInLong.summary: Like pulseIn(), but better for long pulses. Interrupts must be on.

params.state: HIGH to time a high pulse, LOW to time a low pulse.
params.timeout: Longest time to wait in microseconds (default 1000000, one second).

pulseInLong.returns: Pulse length in microseconds, or 0 if no pulse came before the timeout.

shiftOut.summary: Sends a byte one bit at a time, for example to a 74HC595 shift register.

params.clockPin: Pin that is pulsed once per bit.

shiftIn.summary: Reads a byte one bit at a time, for example from a 74HC165 shift register.

params.clockPin: Pin that is pulsed once per bit.

tone.summary: Plays a square-wave tone on a buzzer or speaker. Only one tone plays at a time.

params.pin: Pin the buzzer is connected to.
params.frequency: Pitch in hertz (31 Hz or more).
params.duration: How long to play in milliseconds; 0 (default) plays until noTone().

noTone.summary: Stops the tone started with tone().

params.pin: Pin the tone is playing on.

attachInterrupt.summary: Runs a function immediately when a pin changes, even in the middle of loop(). Keep the function short.

params.interrupt: Interrupt number; use digitalPinToInterrupt(pin). On the Uno only pins 2 and 3 work.
params.isr: Function to run. It takes no arguments and returns nothing.
params.mode: When to trigger: LOW, CHANGE, RISING or FALLING.

detachInterrupt.summary: Turns off an interrupt set with attachInterrupt().

digitalPinToInterrupt.summary: Converts a pin number into the interrupt number attachInterrupt() needs.

params.pin: Pin number (2 or 3 on the Uno).

digitalPinToInterrupt.returns: Interrupt number, or -1 if the pin has no interrupt.

interrupts.summary: Turns interrupts back on after noInterrupts().

noInterrupts.summary: Turns interrupts off so a piece of code is not disturbed. millis() and Serial stop working until interrupts() is called.

map.summary: Rescales a number from one range to another, for example a sensor reading 0 to 1023 into an angle 0 to 180. Uses whole numbers only.

params.fromLow: Lowest value of the input range.
params.fromHigh: Highest value of the input range.
params.toLow: Lowest value of the output range.
params.toHigh: Highest value of the output range.

map.returns: The rescaled value. It is not limited to the output range; use constrain() for that.

constrain.summary: Keeps a number inside a range. Works with any number type.
constrain.returns: low if x is below low, high if x is above high, otherwise x.

min.summary: Picks the smaller of two numbers.

max.summary: Picks the larger of two numbers.

abs.summary: Removes the minus sign of a number.
abs.returns: x if it is positive or zero, otherwise -x.

round.summary: Rounds a number to the nearest whole number; halves round away from zero.
round.returns: The nearest whole number as a long.

pow.summary: Raises a number to a power.

params.exponent: The power, may be a fraction.

pow.returns: base to the power of exponent.

exp.summary: Calculates e (about 2.718) to the power of x.
exp.returns: e to the power of x.

floor.returns: The largest whole number not greater than x.

ceil.returns: The smallest whole number not less than x.

fabs.summary: Absolute value of a decimal number.

sin.summary: Calculates the sine of an angle.

params.rad: Angle in radians; use radians() to convert from degrees.

cos.summary: Calculates the cosine of an angle.

params.rad: Angle in radians; use radians() to convert from degrees.

tan.summary: Calculates the tangent of an angle.

params.rad: Angle in radians; use radians() to convert from degrees.

asin.summary: Inverse sine: finds the angle whose sine is x.
asin.returns: Angle in radians, from -PI/2 to PI/2.

acos.summary: Inverse cosine: finds the angle whose cosine is x.
acos.returns: Angle in radians, from 0 to PI.

atan.summary: Inverse tangent: finds the angle whose tangent is x.
atan.returns: Angle in radians, from -PI/2 to PI/2.

atan2.summary: Finds the angle of the point (x, y) from the x axis, handling all four quadrants. Useful for headings and tilt.
atan2.returns: Angle in radians, from -PI to PI.

random.summary: Picks a pseudo-random whole number. Call randomSeed() first for a different sequence each run.
random.returns: A number from min up to max - 1.

randomSeed.summary: Starts the random number sequence at a new point. analogRead() of an unconnected pin is a common seed.

params.seed: Any number; the same seed gives the same sequence.

bitRead.summary: Reads a single bit of a number.

params.n: Bit position, 0 is the rightmost (least significant) bit.

bitWrite.summary: Sets a single bit of a variable to 0 or 1.

params.n: Bit position, 0 is the rightmost bit.

bitSet.summary: Sets a single bit of a variable to 1.

params.n: Bit position, 0 is the rightmost bit.

bitClear.summary: Clears a single bit of a variable to 0.

params.n: Bit position, 0 is the rightmost bit.

bitToggle.summary: Flips a single bit of a variable: 0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0.

params.n: Bit position, 0 is the rightmost bit.

bit.summary: Makes a number with only one bit set, for use as a mask.
bit.returns: 2 to the power of n (bit(0) is 1, bit(3) is 8).

highByte.summary: Gets the upper 8 bits of a 16-bit number.

lowByte.summary: Gets the lower 8 bits of a number.

makeWord.summary: Joins two bytes into one 16-bit number. word(high, low) does the same.

isAlpha.summary: Checks whether a character is a letter.
isAlpha.returns: true for A to Z and a to z.

isAlphaNumeric.summary: Checks whether a character is a letter or a digit.

isAscii.summary: Checks whether a character is a standard ASCII character.

isControl.summary: Checks whether a character is a control character such as newline or tab.

isDigit.summary: Checks whether a character is a digit.

isGraph.summary: Checks whether a character is visible when printed (not a space).
isGraph.returns: true for printable characters except space.

isHexadecimalDigit.summary: Checks whether a character is a hexadecimal digit.
isHexadecimalDigit.returns: true for 0 to 9, A to F and a to f.

isLowerCase.summary: Checks whether a character is a lowercase letter.

isUpperCase.summary: Checks whether a character is an uppercase letter.

isPrintable.summary: Checks whether a character can be printed, including space.

isPunct.summary: Checks whether a character is punctuation, such as a comma, dot or bracket.

isSpace.summary: Checks whether a character is white space: space, tab, newline, carriage return, vertical tab or form feed.

isWhitespace.summary: Checks whether a character is a space or a tab.

toAscii.summary: Keeps only the lower 7 bits of a character so it becomes standard ASCII.

toLowerCase.returns: The lowercase letter, or c unchanged if it is not an uppercase letter.

toUpperCase.returns: The uppercase letter, or c unchanged if it is not a lowercase letter.

F.summary: Keeps a fixed text in flash memory instead of RAM. The Uno has only 2 KB of RAM, so wrap long print texts in F().
F.returns: The text stored in flash, ready for print() and println().

pinLevel.summary: Pin levels: HIGH is 1 (5 V on the Uno) and LOW is 0 (0 V).

pinModes.summary: Pin modes for pinMode(): INPUT reads a signal, OUTPUT drives a signal, INPUT_PULLUP reads with the internal pull-up resistor so an open button reads HIGH.

LED_BUILTIN.summary: The pin of the small LED on the board (13 on the Uno).

analogPin.summary: Analog input pins A0 to A5. They also work as digital pins 14 to 19 on the Uno.

interruptMode.summary: When attachInterrupt() fires: CHANGE on any change, RISING from LOW to HIGH, FALLING from HIGH to LOW (LOW fires while the pin stays low).

bitOrder.summary: Bit order for shiftOut() and shiftIn(): MSBFIRST sends the highest bit first, LSBFIRST the lowest bit first.

analogReferenceMode.summary: Reference voltages for analogReference(): DEFAULT is 5 V, INTERNAL is 1.1 V, EXTERNAL uses the voltage on the AREF pin (0 to 5 V).

numberBase.summary: Number bases for print() and String(): DEC (base 10), HEX (base 16), OCT (base 8), BIN (base 2).

mathConstant.summary: Math constants: PI (3.14159), HALF_PI, TWO_PI, DEG_TO_RAD and RAD_TO_DEG for angle conversion, and EULER (e, 2.71828).

serialConfig.summary: Serial frame formats for Serial.begin(baud, config): data bits (5 to 8), parity (N none, E even, O odd) and stop bits (1 or 2). The default is SERIAL_8N1.

boolean.summary: Another name for bool: a value that is true or false.

word.summary: An unsigned 16-bit number from 0 to 65535. word(high, low) also builds one from two bytes.

size_t.summary: An unsigned number used for sizes and counts, 0 to 65535 on the Uno.

uint8_t.summary: An unsigned 8-bit number from 0 to 255 (same as byte).

int16_t.summary: A signed 16-bit number from -32768 to 32767 (same as int on the Uno).

int32_t.summary: A signed 32-bit number from about -2.1 billion to 2.1 billion (same as long on the Uno).

uint32_t.summary: An unsigned 32-bit number from 0 to about 4.29 billion (same as unsigned long on the Uno).

int64_t.summary: A signed 64-bit number for very large values. Slow on the Uno and print() cannot show it directly.

uint64_t.summary: An unsigned 64-bit number for very large values. Slow on the Uno and print() cannot show it directly.

Adafruit_BMP280.summary: Creates a BMP280 sensor object on I2C (no arguments) or SPI. Call begin() in setup() before reading it.

begin.summary: Starts the sensor and checks its chip ID.

params.addr: I2C address: 0x77 (default) or 0x76 (used by many breakout boards).

begin.returns: true if the sensor was found.

readPressure.summary: Reads the air pressure. Divide by 100 to get hPa.
readPressure.returns: Pressure in pascals (Pa), about 101325 at sea level.

readAltitude.summary: Works out the height above sea level from the measured pressure.

params.seaLevelhPa: Current sea-level pressure in hPa (default 1013.25); use your local weather value for better accuracy.

seaLevelForAltitude.summary: Works out the sea-level pressure from a known altitude and a pressure reading.

waterBoilingPoint.summary: Works out the temperature at which water boils at a given pressure.

takeForcedMeasurement.summary: In MODE_FORCED, takes one measurement and waits for it to finish.

setSampling.summary: Sets the measuring mode, oversampling, filter and pause between readings.

params.mode: MODE_NORMAL (default, measures continuously), MODE_FORCED (one reading on request) or MODE_SLEEP.
params.tempSampling: Temperature oversampling, SAMPLING_NONE to SAMPLING_X16 (default X16).
params.pressSampling: Pressure oversampling, SAMPLING_NONE to SAMPLING_X16 (default X16).
params.duration: Pause between readings in normal mode, STANDBY_MS_1 (default) to STANDBY_MS_4000.

getStatus.summary: Reads the status register, showing whether a measurement is in progress.

reset.summary: Resets the chip to its power-on settings.

getTemperatureSensor.summary: Gives the temperature part as a separate Adafruit_Sensor.
getTemperatureSensor.returns: Pointer to an Adafruit_Sensor; its events hold temperature in °C.

getPressureSensor.summary: Gives the pressure part as a separate Adafruit_Sensor.
getPressureSensor.returns: Pointer to an Adafruit_Sensor; its events hold pressure in hPa.

address.summary: I2C addresses of the BMP280: 0x77 (BMP280_ADDRESS) and 0x76 (BMP280_ADDRESS_ALT, when the SDO pin is low).

sampling.summary: Oversampling: how many readings are averaged into one, from none (sensor off) to 16. More samples give less noise but take longer. Write as Adafruit_BMP280::SAMPLING_X16.

mode.summary: Power modes: sleep (no readings), forced (one reading, then sleep) or normal (continuous). Write as Adafruit_BMP280::MODE_NORMAL.

filter.summary: Noise filter strength: off, 2, 4, 8 or 16. Stronger filtering smooths out quick changes. Write as Adafruit_BMP280::FILTER_X16.

standby.summary: Pause between readings in normal mode: 1, 63, 125, 250, 500, 1000, 2000 or 4000 ms. Write as Adafruit_BMP280::STANDBY_MS_500.

Adafruit_BusIO_Register.summary: One register (a numbered memory cell) inside an I2C or SPI chip, 1 to 4 bytes wide.

params.i2cdevice: Address of the Adafruit_I2CDevice the register belongs to.
params.spidevice: Address of the Adafruit_SPIDevice the register belongs to.
params.type: How the register number is sent over SPI, one of the Adafruit_BusIO_SPIRegType values.
params.byteorder: LSBFIRST (default) or MSBFIRST for multi-byte registers.
params.address_width: Size of the register number in bytes (default 1).

read.summary: Reads the register. Without arguments it returns the value; the other forms store it in a variable or buffer.

params.buffer: Array that receives the raw bytes.
params.value: Address of a uint8_t or uint16_t that receives the value.

read.returns: The register value, or true on success for the forms with arguments.

readCached.summary: Returns the value from the last read or write without talking to the chip.

write.summary: Writes a value or raw bytes to the register.

params.numbytes: Bytes to write; 0 (default) means the register width.

setAddress.summary: Points the object at a different register.

setAddressWidth.summary: Changes how many bytes the register number takes.

params.address_width: Size of the register number in bytes.

print.summary: Prints the register value in hexadecimal, for debugging.

println.summary: Like print(), then starts a new line.

spiRegType.summary: How a register number is sent over SPI, for example ADDRBIT8_HIGH_TOREAD sets the top bit of the address when reading.

Adafruit_BusIO_RegisterBits.summary: A group of bits inside a register, so you can change a setting without touching the other bits.

params.reg: Address of the Adafruit_BusIO_Register that holds the bits.
params.bits: How many bits the field has.
params.shift: Position of the lowest bit, 0 for the rightmost bit.

write.summary: Writes a value into the bit field, keeping the other bits of the register.

params.value: New value; must fit in the number of bits.

read.returns: Value of the bits, shifted down to start at bit 0.

Adafruit_GFX.summary: Base class for graphics displays. You normally create a display object (such as Adafruit_SSD1306) instead of this.

drawPixel.summary: Sets one pixel to a colour.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

drawLine.summary: Draws a straight line between two points.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.x1: X position of the second point in pixels.
params.y1: Y position of the second point in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

drawRect.summary: Draws the outline of a rectangle; x and y are its top-left corner.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

fillRect.summary: Draws a filled rectangle; x and y are its top-left corner.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

fillScreen.summary: Fills the whole screen with one colour.

params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

drawCircle.summary: Draws the outline of a circle around a centre point.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

fillCircle.summary: Draws a filled circle around a centre point.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

drawCircleHelper.summary: Draws chosen quarters of a circle outline, as used for rounded corners.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.
params.cornername: Bit mask choosing which quarters to draw: 1 top-left, 2 top-right, 4 bottom-right, 8 bottom-left.

fillCircleHelper.summary: Fills chosen halves of a circle, stretched by an extra length; used for rounded rectangles.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.
params.cornername: Which halves to fill: 1 right, 2 left.
params.delta: Extra length in pixels between the two half circles.

drawEllipse.summary: Draws the outline of an ellipse around a centre point.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

fillEllipse.summary: Draws a filled ellipse around a centre point.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

drawTriangle.summary: Draws the outline of a triangle through three corner points.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.x1: X position of the second point in pixels.
params.y1: Y position of the second point in pixels.
params.x2: X position of the third point in pixels.
params.y2: Y position of the third point in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

fillTriangle.summary: Draws a filled triangle through three corner points.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.x1: X position of the second point in pixels.
params.y1: Y position of the second point in pixels.
params.x2: X position of the third point in pixels.
params.y2: Y position of the third point in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

drawRoundRect.summary: Draws the outline of a rectangle with rounded corners.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

fillRoundRect.summary: Draws a filled rectangle with rounded corners.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

drawRotatedRect.summary: Draws the outline of a rectangle turned around its centre.

params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.
params.cenX: X position of the rectangle centre in pixels.
params.cenY: Y position of the rectangle centre in pixels.

fillRotatedRect.summary: Draws a filled rectangle turned around its centre.

params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.
params.cenX: X position of the rectangle centre in pixels.
params.cenY: Y position of the rectangle centre in pixels.

rotatePoint.summary: Rotates a point around the origin (0, 0), changing the given variables.

params.x0: X variable to rotate; receives the new X.
params.y0: Y variable to rotate; receives the new Y.

drawBitmap.summary: Draws a 1-bit image: set bits use the colour, clear bits are skipped or drawn in bg.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.bitmap: Array of image bytes, usually stored in PROGMEM.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.
params.bg: Background colour drawn behind the set pixels.

drawXBitmap.summary: Draws a 1-bit image saved in XBM format (for example exported from GIMP).

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.bitmap: Array of image bytes, usually stored in PROGMEM.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

drawGrayscaleBitmap.summary: Draws an 8-bit grayscale image, one byte per pixel, for colour displays.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.bitmap: Array of image bytes, usually stored in PROGMEM.
params.mask: 1-bit mask array; only pixels whose mask bit is 1 are drawn.

drawRGBBitmap.summary: Draws a 16-bit colour image (RGB565), one value per pixel, for colour displays.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.bitmap: Array of image bytes, usually stored in PROGMEM.
params.mask: 1-bit mask array; only pixels whose mask bit is 1 are drawn.

drawChar.summary: Draws one character at a position without moving the text cursor.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.
params.bg: Background colour drawn behind the set pixels.
params.size: Scale factor; 1 is 6x8 pixels per character.

setCursor.summary: Moves the text cursor; the next print() starts here.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).

setTextColor.summary: Sets the text colour. With only one colour the background stays transparent.

params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.
params.bg: Background colour drawn behind the set pixels.

setTextSize.summary: Makes text bigger by a whole-number factor; size 1 is 6x8 pixels per character.

setTextWrap.summary: Chooses whether long text continues on the next line or is cut off at the right edge.

params.wrap: true to wrap (default), false to clip.

setFont.summary: Chooses a font from the Fonts folder, or the built-in 6x8 font when called with no argument.

params.font: Address of a GFXfont, for example &FreeSans9pt7b.

cp437.summary: Switches the built-in font to the correct Code Page 437 character numbers.

params.enable: true for correct CP437 codes, false for the old layout.

getTextBounds.summary: Measures the box a piece of text would cover if printed at x, y, without drawing it.

params.x: Cursor X position to measure from.
params.y: Cursor Y position to measure from.
params.x1: Receives the left edge of the box.
params.y1: Receives the top edge of the box.
params.w: Receives the box width in pixels.
params.h: Receives the box height in pixels.

getCursorX.summary: Reads the X position of the text cursor.

getCursorY.summary: Reads the Y position of the text cursor.

setRotation.summary: Rotates everything drawn afterwards in steps of 90 degrees.

width.summary: Reads the screen width, taking rotation into account.

height.summary: Reads the screen height, taking rotation into account.

invertDisplay.summary: Swaps light and dark pixels on the whole screen, without changing what is drawn.

params.invert: true to invert, false for normal.

startWrite.summary: Begins a batch of write... calls; advanced, for faster drawing.

writePixel.summary: Sets one pixel inside a startWrite() / endWrite() batch.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

writeFillRect.summary: Draws a filled rectangle inside a startWrite() / endWrite() batch.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

writeFastHLine.summary: Draws a horizontal line inside a startWrite() / endWrite() batch.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

writeFastVLine.summary: Draws a vertical line inside a startWrite() / endWrite() batch.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

writeLine.summary: Draws a line inside a startWrite() / endWrite() batch.

params.x0: X position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.y0: Y position of the first point (or centre) in pixels.
params.x1: X position of the second point in pixels.
params.y1: Y position of the second point in pixels.
params.color: Colour to draw with; on an SSD1306 use SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK or SSD1306_INVERSE.

endWrite.summary: Ends a batch started with startWrite().

Adafruit_I2CDevice.summary: Describes a chip on the I2C bus. Call begin() before reading or writing.

params.addr: 7-bit I2C address of the chip, for example 0x68.

begin.summary: Starts the I2C bus and, by default, checks that the chip answers.

params.addr_detect: true (default) to check that the chip responds at its address.

begin.returns: true if the chip was found (or detection was skipped).

end.summary: Stops using the device and releases the bus.

detected.summary: Checks whether the chip answers at its address.

address.summary: Gets the I2C address of the device.

read.summary: Reads bytes from the chip into a buffer.

params.stop: true (default) to release the bus when done.

read.returns: true if all bytes were read.

write.summary: Writes bytes to the chip, optionally sending a prefix (such as a register number) first.

params.stop: true (default) to release the bus when done.

write.returns: true if the chip acknowledged the data.

write_then_read.summary: Writes some bytes, then reads a reply. Typical use: send a register number, then read its value.

params.stop: true to release the bus between the write and the read (default false).

params.desiredclk: Clock in Hz, for example 100000 or 400000.

setSpeed.returns: true if the speed could be set.

maxBufferSize.summary: Largest number of bytes that can be sent or read in one go.
maxBufferSize.returns: Buffer size in bytes (32 on the Uno).

Adafruit_MPU6050.summary: Creates an MPU6050 sensor object. Call begin() in setup() before reading it.

begin.summary: Starts the I2C bus and checks that the MPU6050 answers.

params.i2c_addr: I2C address: 0x68 (default, AD0 pin low) or 0x69 (AD0 pin high).
params.sensorID: Your own ID number for the sensor (default 0).

begin.returns: true if the sensor was found.

getEvent.summary: Reads acceleration, rotation and temperature all at once.

params.accel: Event that receives acceleration in m/s², in accel.acceleration.x, .y and .z.
params.gyro: Event that receives rotation speed in rad/s, in gyro.gyro.x, .y and .z.
params.temp: Event that receives the chip temperature in °C, in temp.temperature.

setAccelerometerRange.summary: Sets the largest acceleration the sensor can measure. A smaller range gives finer readings.

setGyroRange.summary: Sets the fastest rotation the sensor can measure.

params.range: MPU6050_RANGE_250_DEG (default), _500_DEG, _1000_DEG or _2000_DEG, in degrees per second.

setFilterBandwidth.summary: Sets the built-in low-pass filter. A lower bandwidth gives smoother but slower readings.

params.bandwidth: MPU6050_BAND_260_HZ (filter almost off) down to MPU6050_BAND_5_HZ.

getFilterBandwidth.summary: Gets the current low-pass filter setting.

setHighPassFilter.summary: Sets the high-pass filter used by motion detection, which ignores slow changes such as gravity.

getHighPassFilter.summary: Gets the current high-pass filter setting.

setMotionInterrupt.summary: Turns motion detection on or off. When motion is detected, the INT pin is signalled.

setMotionDetectionThreshold.summary: Sets how strong a movement must be to count as motion.

params.thr: Threshold from 0 to 255, about 2 mg per step.

setMotionDetectionDuration.summary: Sets how long a movement must last to count as motion.

getMotionInterruptStatus.summary: Checks whether motion was detected since the last check.

setInterruptPinPolarity.summary: Chooses whether the INT pin goes HIGH or LOW when an interrupt happens.

params.active_low: true for LOW when active, false (default) for HIGH.

setInterruptPinLatch.summary: Chooses whether the INT pin stays active until read, or only gives a short pulse.

params.held: true to hold the pin until the status is read, false for a 50 µs pulse.

setFsyncSampleOutput.summary: Chooses which reading records the state of the FSYNC pin (advanced).

params.fsync_output: One of the MPU6050_FSYNC_OUT_… values; MPU6050_FSYNC_OUT_DISABLED turns it off.

setI2CBypass.summary: Connects the auxiliary I2C pins (XDA, XCL) directly to the main bus, to reach a sensor wired to them.

setClock.summary: Chooses the clock source of the chip (advanced).

params.clock: One of the MPU6050_INTR_8MHz or MPU6050_PLL_… values.

getClock.returns: One of the clock select values.

setSampleRateDivisor.summary: Slows down how often new readings are produced. Sample rate = 1 kHz (or 8 kHz with the filter off) divided by divisor + 1.

enableSleep.summary: Puts the sensor to sleep to save power, or wakes it up.

params.enable: true to sleep, false to wake.

enableSleep.returns: true if the setting was written.

enableCycle.summary: Low-power mode where the sensor wakes up now and then to take one accelerometer reading.

params.enable: true to turn cycle mode on.

enableCycle.returns: true if the setting was written.

setCycleRate.summary: Sets how often the sensor wakes up in cycle mode.

getCycleRate.summary: Gets the cycle mode wake-up rate.

setGyroStandby.summary: Switches off single gyroscope axes to save power.

params.xAxisStandby: true to switch off the X axis.
params.yAxisStandby: true to switch off the Y axis.
params.zAxisStandby: true to switch off the Z axis.

setGyroStandby.returns: true if the setting was written.

setAccelerometerStandby.summary: Switches off single accelerometer axes to save power.

params.xAxisStandby: true to switch off the X axis.
params.yAxisStandby: true to switch off the Y axis.
params.zAxisStandby: true to switch off the Z axis.

setAccelerometerStandby.returns: true if the setting was written.

setTemperatureStandby.summary: Switches the temperature sensor off or on.
setTemperatureStandby.returns: true if the setting was written.

reset.summary: Resets the chip to its power-on settings.

getTemperatureSensor.summary: Gives the temperature part as a separate Adafruit_Sensor.
getTemperatureSensor.returns: Pointer to an Adafruit_Sensor; use its getEvent().

getAccelerometerSensor.summary: Gives the accelerometer as a separate Adafruit_Sensor.
getAccelerometerSensor.returns: Pointer to an Adafruit_Sensor; use its getEvent().

getGyroSensor.summary: Gives the gyroscope as a separate Adafruit_Sensor.
getGyroSensor.returns: Pointer to an Adafruit_Sensor; use its getEvent().

MPU6050_I2CADDR_DEFAULT.summary: Default I2C address of the MPU6050, 0x68 (AD0 pin low).

accelRange.summary: Accelerometer ranges: ±2, ±4, ±8 or ±16 g. ±2 g is the default and the most precise.

gyroRange.summary: Gyroscope ranges: ±250, ±500, ±1000 or ±2000 degrees per second. ±250 is the default.

bandwidth.summary: Low-pass filter bandwidths: 260, 184, 94, 44, 21, 10 or 5 Hz. Lower means smoother but slower to react.

highpass.summary: High-pass filter settings for motion detection: off, 5, 2.5, 1.25 or 0.63 Hz, or hold.

cycleRate.summary: Wake-up rates for low-power cycle mode: 1.25, 5, 20 or 40 Hz.

fsyncOut.summary: Which reading records the FSYNC pin state: disabled, temperature, a gyro axis or an accelerometer axis.

clockSelect.summary: Clock sources: the internal 8 MHz oscillator, a gyro axis PLL (more stable), an external clock, or stop.

Adafruit_NeoPixel.summary: Creates an LED strip object. Call begin() in setup() before using it.

params.n: Number of LEDs on the strip.
params.pin: Digital pin connected to the strip data input (default 6).
params.type: Colour order plus speed, for example NEO_GRB + NEO_KHZ800 (most WS2812 strips).

begin.summary: Prepares the data pin. Call once in setup().
begin.returns: true if the strip memory was set up.

show.summary: Sends the stored colours to the LEDs. Changes appear only after calling this.

setPixelColor.summary: Stores a colour for one LED; call show() to light it.

params.n: Index of the LED, starting at 0 for the first one.
params.color: Packed colour from Color() or ColorHSV().

getPixelColor.summary: Reads the colour stored for one LED.

params.n: Index of the LED, starting at 0 for the first one.

getPixelColor.returns: Packed colour, or 0 if n is out of range.

fill.summary: Sets many LEDs to one colour; with no count it fills to the end of the strip.

params.color: Packed colour (default 0, off).
params.first: Index of the first LED to fill (default 0).
params.count: How many LEDs to fill; 0 means up to the end.

clear.summary: Sets every LED to off in memory; call show() to apply.

setBrightness.summary: Scales the brightness of the whole strip. Best called once in setup().

getBrightness.summary: Reads the brightness set with setBrightness().

numPixels.summary: Reads how many LEDs the strip has.

setPin.summary: Changes the data pin after the object was created.

params.pin: New digital pin for the strip data.

getPin.summary: Reads the data pin in use.
getPin.returns: Pin number, or -1 if none is set.

updateLength.summary: Changes the number of LEDs; clears all colours.

updateType.summary: Changes the colour order and speed of the strip.

params.type: New type, for example NEO_GRB + NEO_KHZ800.

canShow.summary: Checks whether enough time (about 300 µs) has passed since the last show().
canShow.returns: true if show() can send now without waiting.

getPixels.summary: Gives direct access to the raw colour bytes (advanced).
getPixels.returns: Pointer to 3 or 4 bytes per LED, in the strip colour order.

rainbow.summary: Fills the strip with a rainbow of colours; call show() to display it.

params.firstHue: Hue of the first LED, 0 to 65535 (default 0, red).
params.reps: How many full rainbows fit along the strip (default 1).
params.gammify: true to apply gamma correction for more natural colours (default).

Color.summary: Packs red, green, blue (and white) values into one colour number.

ColorHSV.summary: Makes a colour from hue, saturation and value, handy for rainbows and fades.

params.hue: Hue from 0 to 65535 around the colour wheel: 0 red, about 21845 green, about 43690 blue.

gamma32.summary: Applies gamma correction to a packed colour so it looks more natural to the eye.

params.color: Packed colour to correct.

gamma8.summary: Applies gamma correction to one brightness value.

sine8.summary: Fast 8-bit sine wave, useful for smooth pulsing effects.

params.x: Angle, 0 to 255 for one full turn.

sine8.returns: Sine value, 0 to 255 (128 at the middle).

colorOrder.summary: Order in which the LEDs expect colour bytes. Most WS2812 strips use NEO_GRB; W variants are for RGBW strips.

speed.summary: Data speed: NEO_KHZ800 for WS2812 and most strips, NEO_KHZ400 for old WS2811 LEDs. Add it to the colour order.

Adafruit_Sensor.summary: Base class of all Adafruit unified sensors. You do not create one yourself; drivers such as Adafruit_MPU6050 hand you an Adafruit_Sensor pointer.

getEvent.summary: Takes a new reading and stores it in an event structure.

params.event: Address of a sensors_event_t that receives the reading, for example &e.

getEvent.returns: true if a reading was taken.

getSensor.summary: Fills a sensor_t with details about the sensor, such as its name, range and resolution.

params.sensor: Address of a sensor_t to fill, for example &s.

enableAutoRange.summary: Lets the sensor change its range by itself for more precise readings, if it supports that.

params.enabled: true to turn auto-ranging on, false to turn it off.

printSensorDetails.summary: Prints the sensor name, type, range and resolution to Serial.

sensors_event_t.summary: One sensor reading. Read the field that matches the sensor: event.temperature in °C, event.pressure in hPa, event.relative_humidity in %, event.acceleration.x / .y / .z in m/s², event.gyro.x / .y / .z in rad/s, event.magnetic in µT, event.distance in cm, event.light in lux. event.timestamp is in milliseconds.

sensors_vec_t.summary: A 3-axis value inside an event. Use x, y and z (or v[0] to v[2]); orientation sensors use roll, pitch and heading in degrees instead.

sensor_t.summary: Information about a sensor: name, version, sensor_id, type, min_value and max_value (its range in SI units), resolution, and min_delay in microseconds between readings.

gravity.summary: Gravity in m/s²: on Earth 9.80665 (also SENSORS_GRAVITY_STANDARD), on the Moon 1.6 and on the Sun 275. Divide an acceleration by SENSORS_GRAVITY_EARTH to get g.

magfield.summary: Strongest and weakest magnetic field at the surface of the Earth, 60 and 30 µT.

SENSORS_PRESSURE_SEALEVELHPA.summary: Average air pressure at sea level, 1013.25 hPa. Handy as the reference for altitude calculations.

conversion.summary: Unit multipliers: degrees/s to rad/s (0.01745), rad/s to degrees/s (57.296) and gauss to µT (100). Example: g.gyro.z * SENSORS_RADS_TO_DPS gives degrees per second.

sensorType.summary: Kind of sensor, found in sensor_t.type and sensors_event_t.type, for example SENSOR_TYPE_ACCELEROMETER or SENSOR_TYPE_AMBIENT_TEMPERATURE.

Adafruit_SPIDevice.summary: Describes a chip on the SPI bus, using hardware SPI or any pins you choose (software SPI). Call begin() before use.

params.dataMode: SPI mode, SPI_MODE0 to SPI_MODE3 (default SPI_MODE0).

begin.summary: Sets up the pins and the SPI bus.

read.summary: Reads bytes from the chip into a buffer.

write.summary: Writes bytes to the chip, optionally sending a prefix first.

write_then_read.summary: Writes some bytes, then reads a reply, all while chip-select stays active.

write_and_read.summary: Sends the bytes in a buffer and replaces each with the byte received at the same time.

params.buffer: Bytes to send; overwritten with the bytes received.

transfer.summary: Exchanges one byte, or a whole buffer, with the chip. Call between beginTransaction() and endTransaction().

params.buffer: Bytes to send; overwritten with the bytes received.

beginTransaction.summary: Claims the SPI bus with this device's speed and mode settings.

beginTransactionWithAssertingCS.summary: Claims the SPI bus and pulls chip-select LOW to select the device.

endTransactionWithDeassertingCS.summary: Sets chip-select HIGH again and releases the SPI bus.

bitOrder.summary: SPI bit order: most significant bit first (the usual choice) or least significant bit first.

Adafruit_SSD1306.summary: Creates an OLED display object. The first form is for I2C (the usual 4-pin module); the others are for SPI modules.

params.rstPin: Reset pin, or -1 if the module has none (shares the Arduino reset).
params.clkDuring: I2C speed in Hz while talking to the display (default 400000).
params.clkAfter: I2C speed in Hz restored afterwards (default 100000).
params.mosiPin: Data (MOSI / D1) pin for software SPI.
params.sclkPin: Clock (SCK / D0) pin for software SPI.

begin.summary: Starts the display and reserves its screen buffer (1 KB for 128x64). Call it once in setup().

params.vcc: Power source: SSD1306_SWITCHCAPVCC for most modules, or SSD1306_EXTERNALVCC.
params.address: I2C address, usually 0x3C (sometimes 0x3D); 0 picks one from the screen height.
params.reset: true to pulse the reset pin first (default).
params.periphBegin: true to also start the Wire or SPI bus (default).

begin.returns: true if it worked, false if the display was not found or memory ran out.

display.summary: Sends the drawing buffer to the screen. Nothing you draw appears until you call this.

clearDisplay.summary: Clears the drawing buffer to black. Call display() to show the empty screen.

dim.summary: Lowers or restores the screen brightness.

params.dim: true for dim, false for normal brightness.

startscrollright.summary: Starts scrolling rows of the screen to the right, done by the display itself.

params.start: First page (row of 8 pixels) to scroll, 0 to 7 on a 64-pixel screen.

startscrollleft.summary: Starts scrolling rows of the screen to the left.

params.start: First page (row of 8 pixels) to scroll, 0 to 7 on a 64-pixel screen.

startscrolldiagright.summary: Starts scrolling diagonally up and to the right.

params.start: First page (row of 8 pixels) to scroll, 0 to 7 on a 64-pixel screen.

startscrolldiagleft.summary: Starts scrolling diagonally up and to the left.

params.start: First page (row of 8 pixels) to scroll, 0 to 7 on a 64-pixel screen.

stopscroll.summary: Stops any scrolling. Call display() afterwards to redraw the buffer.

ssd1306_command.summary: Sends one raw command byte to the controller chip (advanced).

params.command: Command byte from the SSD1306 datasheet, such as SSD1306_SETCONTRAST.

getPixel.summary: Reads one pixel from the drawing buffer.

params.x: X position in pixels, counted from the left edge (0).
params.y: Y position in pixels, counted from the top edge (0).

getPixel.returns: true if the pixel is on (white).

getBuffer.summary: Gives direct access to the drawing buffer (advanced).
getBuffer.returns: Pointer to the buffer bytes, 8 vertical pixels per byte.

vcc.summary: Display power source for begin(): SWITCHCAPVCC makes the panel voltage from 3.3 V (most modules); EXTERNALVCC uses an outside supply.

color.summary: Pixel colours: WHITE turns pixels on, BLACK turns them off, INVERSE flips them.

legacyColor.summary: Older short names for SSD1306_WHITE, SSD1306_BLACK and SSD1306_INVERSE.

command.summary: Raw controller commands for ssd1306_command(), such as turning the panel on or off or setting contrast.

DallasTemperature.summary: Creates a thermometer manager on a OneWire bus. Call begin() in setup().

params.oneWire: Address of the OneWire bus the sensors are on, for example &oneWire.
params.pullupPin: Pin that switches an external pull-up resistor, if you use one.

begin.summary: Searches the bus and counts the connected sensors.

setOneWire.summary: Sets the OneWire bus, for an object created without one.

setPullupPin.summary: Sets the pin that switches an external pull-up during conversions.

getDeviceCount.summary: Number of 1-Wire devices found by begin().

getDS18Count.summary: Number of DS18-family thermometers found by begin().

verifyDeviceCount.summary: Searches the bus again and updates the device count if it changed.
verifyDeviceCount.returns: true if the count is unchanged.

validAddress.summary: Checks the CRC of an address.
validAddress.returns: true if the address is valid.

validFamily.summary: Checks whether an address belongs to a supported thermometer model.
validFamily.returns: true if the model is supported.

getAddress.summary: Gets the address of the sensor at a given position on the bus.
getAddress.returns: true if a sensor was found at that position.

isConnected.summary: Checks whether a sensor is still answering.

params.scratchPad: Optional 9-byte array that receives the sensor memory.

readScratchPad.summary: Reads the 9-byte working memory (scratchpad) of a sensor (advanced).

writeScratchPad.summary: Writes alarm limits and settings to the scratchpad of a sensor (advanced).

readPowerSupply.summary: Checks whether a sensor runs on parasite power (only 2 wires).

params.deviceAddress: 8-byte device address, or nothing to ask all sensors.

readPowerSupply.returns: true if parasite power is used.

isParasitePowerMode.summary: Checks whether any sensor on the bus uses parasite power.
isParasitePowerMode.returns: true if parasite power is used.

getResolution.summary: Gets the resolution in bits, for all sensors or for one.

setResolution.summary: Sets the resolution: 9 bits (0.5 °C, about 94 ms) up to 12 bits (0.0625 °C, about 750 ms).

params.deviceAddress: 8-byte device address, to set only one sensor.
params.skipGlobalBitResolutionCalculation: true to leave the shared setting unchanged (default false).

setResolution.returns: true on success (form with an address).

setWaitForConversion.summary: Chooses whether requestTemperatures() waits until the reading is ready.

params.flag: true (default) to wait, false to return at once so the sketch can do other work.

getWaitForConversion.summary: Checks whether requestTemperatures() waits for the reading.

setCheckForConversion.summary: Chooses whether to ask the sensor if it is done, instead of waiting a fixed time.

isConversionComplete.summary: Checks whether the requested temperature readings are ready.

millisToWaitForConversion.summary: How long a reading takes at a resolution.

params.bitResolution: Resolution, 9 to 12 bits; without it, the current resolution is used.

blockTillConversionComplete.summary: Waits until a requested reading is ready.

params.bitResolution: Resolution in bits, which sets the longest wait.
params.start: millis() value when the request was sent.

requestTemperatures.summary: Tells all sensors to measure the temperature. Read the results afterwards with getTempCByIndex() or getTempC().
requestTemperatures.returns: A result that is true if the request was sent.

requestTemperaturesByAddress.summary: Tells one sensor to measure the temperature.
requestTemperaturesByAddress.returns: A result that is true if the request was sent.

requestTemperaturesByIndex.summary: Tells the sensor at a position on the bus to measure the temperature.
requestTemperaturesByIndex.returns: A result that is true if the request was sent.

getTempCByIndex.summary: Reads the temperature of the sensor at a position on the bus. Call requestTemperatures() first.
getTempCByIndex.returns: Temperature in °C, or DEVICE_DISCONNECTED_C (-127) if there is no sensor.

getTempFByIndex.returns: Temperature in °F, or DEVICE_DISCONNECTED_F (-196.6) if there is no sensor.

getTempC.summary: Reads the temperature of one sensor by its address. Call requestTemperatures() first.

params.retryCount: Extra attempts if the read fails (default 0).

getTempC.returns: Temperature in °C, or DEVICE_DISCONNECTED_C (-127) on failure.

getTempF.returns: Temperature in °F, or DEVICE_DISCONNECTED_F (-196.6) on failure.

getTemp.summary: Reads the raw temperature value of one sensor; convert it with rawToCelsius().

params.retryCount: Extra attempts if the read fails (default 0).

getTemp.returns: Raw value in 1/128 °C, or DEVICE_DISCONNECTED_RAW on failure.

saveScratchPad.summary: Stores the alarm limits and resolution in the sensor EEPROM so they survive power-off.

params.deviceAddress: 8-byte device address, or nothing for all sensors.

saveScratchPadByIndex.summary: Like saveScratchPad(), for the sensor at a position on the bus.

recallScratchPad.summary: Loads the saved settings from the sensor EEPROM back into its working memory.

params.deviceAddress: 8-byte device address, or nothing for all sensors.

recallScratchPadByIndex.summary: Like recallScratchPad(), for the sensor at a position on the bus.

setAutoSaveScratchPad.summary: Chooses whether setting changes are saved to the sensor EEPROM automatically.

setHighAlarmTemp.summary: Sets the upper alarm limit of a sensor.

setLowAlarmTemp.summary: Sets the lower alarm limit of a sensor.

getHighAlarmTemp.summary: Gets the upper alarm limit of a sensor.

getLowAlarmTemp.summary: Gets the lower alarm limit of a sensor.

resetAlarmSearch.summary: Restarts alarmSearch() from the first device.

alarmSearch.summary: Finds the next sensor whose last reading was outside its alarm limits.

params.newAddr: 8-byte array that receives the address found.

alarmSearch.returns: true if a sensor in alarm was found.

hasAlarm.summary: Checks whether any sensor, or one sensor, is in alarm.

processAlarms.summary: Calls the alarm handler for each sensor that is in alarm.

setAlarmHandler.summary: Sets the function called by processAlarms() for each sensor in alarm.

params.handler: Function of the form void name(const uint8_t *deviceAddress).

hasAlarmHandler.summary: Checks whether an alarm handler is set.

setUserData.summary: Stores your own 16-bit number in the alarm bytes of a sensor (when alarms are not used).

setUserDataByIndex.summary: Like setUserData(), for the sensor at a position on the bus.

getUserData.summary: Reads the number stored with setUserData().

getUserDataByIndex.summary: Like getUserData(), for the sensor at a position on the bus.

rawToCelsius.summary: Converts a raw value from getTemp() to Celsius.

rawToFahrenheit.summary: Converts a raw value from getTemp() to Fahrenheit.

celsiusToRaw.summary: Converts Celsius to the raw format.

DeviceAddress.summary: An 8-byte array holding the unique address of one sensor. The first byte is the family code, the last is a CRC.

disconnected.summary: Values returned when a sensor does not answer: -127 °C, -196.6 °F, or -7040 raw. Compare a reading with DEVICE_DISCONNECTED_C to detect a missing sensor.

faultC.summary: Error readings in °C: open circuit (-254), data shorted to GND (-253) or to VDD (-252), power-on reset value (-251), not enough power (-250).

model.summary: Family codes of supported sensors (first address byte): DS18S20 0x10, DS18B20 0x28, DS1822 0x22, DS1825 0x3B, DS28EA00 0x42.

DHT.summary: Creates a DHT sensor object. Call begin() in setup() before reading it.

params.pin: Digital pin the sensor data wire is connected to.
params.type: Sensor model: DHT11, DHT12, DHT21, DHT22 or AM2301.

begin.summary: Prepares the data pin. Wait at least 2 seconds (1 s for DHT11) between readings.

params.usec: How long to pull the line up before reading, in microseconds (default 55).

readTemperature.summary: Reads the temperature. Returns NAN if the reading failed, so check it with isnan().

params.force: true to read the sensor now even if the last reading is less than 2 seconds old.

readTemperature.returns: Temperature in °C or °F, or NAN on failure.

readHumidity.summary: Reads the relative humidity. Returns NAN if the reading failed.

params.force: true to read the sensor now even if the last reading is less than 2 seconds old.

readHumidity.returns: Relative humidity in percent (0 to 100), or NAN on failure.

read.summary: Reads raw data from the sensor. readTemperature() and readHumidity() call this for you.

params.force: true to read now even if the last reading is less than 2 seconds old.

read.returns: true if the data was read correctly.

computeHeatIndex.summary: Works out the heat index, how hot it feels when humidity is taken into account. Given only isFahrenheit, it reads the sensor itself.

params.temperature: Air temperature, in °F or °C as set by isFahrenheit.
params.isFahrenheit: true (default) if temperature is in °F and the result should be too, false for °C.

sensorType.summary: Sensor models for the constructor: DHT11 (blue, 0 to 50 °C), DHT12, DHT21 or AM2301 (same value), and DHT22 (white, more precise, -40 to 80 °C).

EEPROMClass.summary: The EEPROM memory class. You do not create it yourself: use the ready-made EEPROM object.

instance.summary: The built-in EEPROM memory (1024 bytes on the Uno, addresses 0 to 1023). EEPROM[address] also reads and writes one byte.

params.address: Byte address, from 0 to 1023 on the Uno.

read.returns: The stored byte (0 to 255); 255 if never written.

write.summary: Writes one byte to EEPROM. Each cell wears out after about 100000 writes, so prefer update().

params.address: Byte address, from 0 to 1023 on the Uno.

update.summary: Writes one byte only if it differs from what is stored, which saves EEPROM wear.

params.address: Byte address, from 0 to 1023 on the Uno.

get.summary: Reads any variable or struct (int, float, ...) starting at an address.

params.data: Variable to fill; its size decides how many bytes are read.

put.summary: Stores any variable or struct starting at an address. Only changed bytes are written.

params.data: Variable to store; it uses sizeof(data) bytes.

length.summary: Gets the size of the EEPROM.
length.returns: Number of bytes (1024 on the Uno).

instance.summary: The serial port connected to USB and to pins 0 (RX) and 1 (TX). Use it to talk to the Serial Monitor.

begin.summary: Opens the serial port. Call it in setup() and choose the same speed in the Serial Monitor.

params.baud: Speed in bits per second, for example 9600 or 115200.

end.summary: Closes the serial port so pins 0 and 1 can be used as normal pins.

availableForWrite.summary: Checks how many bytes can be written without waiting.
availableForWrite.returns: Free space in the send buffer in bytes (up to 63 on the Uno).

flush.summary: Waits until all outgoing data has been sent.

Keypad.summary: Creates a keypad from a key map and the pins of its rows and columns.

params.rowPins: Array of pins connected to the rows.
params.colPins: Array of pins connected to the columns.

makeKeymap.summary: Turns a 2D array of characters into a key map for the Keypad constructor.

params.keys: 2D char array with one character per key, row by row.

makeKeymap.returns: The key map to pass to Keypad.

getKey.summary: Checks the keypad once without waiting. Call it often, for example in every loop().
getKey.returns: The character of a newly pressed key, or NO_KEY if none.

getKeys.summary: Scans for several keys pressed together (up to 10). The results are in the key list of the keypad.
getKeys.returns: true if any key changed state.

getState.summary: Gets the state of the last key that changed.

begin.summary: Switches to a different key map, for example for a second layer of keys.

params.userKeymap: New key layout, made with makeKeymap(keys).

isPressed.summary: Checks whether a key is currently pressed. Use after getKeys().

params.keyChar: Character of the key to check.

isPressed.returns: true if that key is pressed.

setDebounceTime.summary: Sets how long a key must be stable before it counts, to ignore contact bounce (default 10 ms).

setHoldTime.summary: Sets how long a key must be held before its state becomes HOLD (default 500 ms).

addEventListener.summary: Sets a function to run whenever a key changes state. Inside it, getState() tells what happened.

params.listener: Function taking the key character, for example void keypadEvent(KeypadEvent key).

findInList.summary: Looks for a key in the list of active keys filled by getKeys().

params.keyChar: Character of the key to find.
params.keyCode: Code of the key to find (row times columns plus column).

findInList.returns: Position in the list (0 to 9), or -1 if not found.

waitForKey.summary: Waits until a key is pressed. Nothing else in the sketch runs while it waits.
waitForKey.returns: The character of the pressed key.

keyStateChanged.summary: Checks whether the state of the current key just changed.

numKeys.summary: Counts the keys in the active list after getKeys().

KeyState.summary: Type of a key state: IDLE, PRESSED, HOLD or RELEASED.

KeypadEvent.summary: Type of the key character passed to an event listener (a char).

states.summary: Key states: IDLE (not pressed), PRESSED (just pressed), HOLD (held past the hold time), RELEASED (just let go).

NO_KEY.summary: The empty character returned by getKey() when no key was pressed.

LiquidCrystal_I2C.summary: Creates an LCD object for a display with an I2C backpack. Call init() in setup().

params.address: I2C address of the backpack, usually 0x27 or 0x3F.
params.cols: Number of characters per row, for example 16 or 20.
params.rows: Number of rows, for example 2 or 4.

init.summary: Starts I2C and sets up the LCD. Call once in setup().

begin.summary: Sets up the LCD with a size; init() already does this for you.

clear.summary: Erases the screen and moves the cursor to the top-left corner.

home.summary: Moves the cursor to the top-left corner without erasing.

setCursor.summary: Moves the cursor; the next print() starts here.

params.col: Column, starting at 0 on the left.
params.row: Row, starting at 0 at the top.

setBacklight.summary: Turns the backlight on or off from a value.

params.value: 0 for off, any other value for on.

display.summary: Shows the text again after noDisplay().

noDisplay.summary: Hides the text without erasing it.

scrollDisplayLeft.summary: Shifts all text one position to the left.

scrollDisplayRight.summary: Shifts all text one position to the right.

leftToRight.summary: New text is written from left to right (default).

rightToLeft.summary: New text is written from right to left.

autoscroll.summary: Shifts the existing text for each new character, so the cursor stays still.

createChar.summary: Defines a custom 5x8 character; show it with write(location).

params.charmap: 8 bytes, one per row from top; the low 5 bits are the pixels.

command.summary: Sends a raw command byte to the LCD controller (advanced).

printstr.summary: Prints a text string; same as print().

params.charmap: 8 bytes, one per row from top; the low 5 bits are the pixels.

charsize.summary: Character size for begin(): 5x8 dots (normal) or 5x10 dots (some one-row LCDs).

NewPing.summary: Creates a sensor on a trigger pin and an echo pin. Use the same pin twice for 3-pin sensors.

params.trigger_pin: Pin connected to the sensor TRIG.
params.echo_pin: Pin connected to the sensor ECHO.
params.max_cm_distance: Farthest distance to wait for, in centimetres (default 500).

ping.summary: Sends one ping and measures how long the echo takes.

params.max_cm_distance: Optional new maximum distance in centimetres; 0 keeps the one from the constructor.

ping.returns: Echo time in microseconds, or 0 if nothing is in range.

ping_cm.summary: Sends one ping and gives the distance in centimetres.

params.max_cm_distance: Optional new maximum distance in centimetres; 0 keeps the one from the constructor.

ping_cm.returns: Distance in whole centimetres, or 0 if nothing is in range.

ping_in.summary: Sends one ping and gives the distance in inches.

params.max_cm_distance: Optional new maximum distance in centimetres; 0 keeps the one from the constructor.

ping_in.returns: Distance in whole inches, or 0 if nothing is in range.

ping_median.summary: Sends several pings and keeps the middle result, which filters out bad readings. Takes about 30 ms per ping.

params.max_cm_distance: Optional new maximum distance in centimetres; 0 keeps the one from the constructor.

ping_median.returns: Median echo time in microseconds; convert it with convert_cm() or convert_in().

convert_cm.summary: Turns an echo time into centimetres.

params.echoTime: Echo time in microseconds, from ping() or ping_median().

convert_in.summary: Turns an echo time into inches.

params.echoTime: Echo time in microseconds, from ping() or ping_median().

ping_timer.summary: Starts a ping in the background using Timer2, so loop() keeps running. Your function is called every 24 µs until the echo arrives.

params.userFunc: Function with no parameters that calls check_timer().
params.max_cm_distance: Optional new maximum distance in centimetres; 0 keeps the one from the constructor.

check_timer.summary: Call inside your ping_timer() function to see if the echo has arrived. The echo time is then in ping_result (µs).
check_timer.returns: true once the echo has been received.

timer_us.summary: Runs a function repeatedly every few microseconds using Timer2. This can break tone() and PWM on pins 3 and 11.

params.userFunc: Function with no parameters to call.

timer_ms.summary: Runs a function repeatedly every few milliseconds using Timer2. This can break tone() and PWM on pins 3 and 11.

params.userFunc: Function with no parameters to call.

timer_stop.summary: Stops the Timer2 interval started by timer_us(), timer_ms() or ping_timer().

MAX_SENSOR_DISTANCE.summary: Default and largest maximum distance: 500 cm.

NO_ECHO.summary: Value 0, returned when no echo comes back within the maximum distance.

roundTrip.summary: Microseconds the sound needs to travel 1 unit and back: 57 µs per cm, 146 µs per inch.

OneWire.summary: Creates a 1-Wire bus on a pin. The data line needs a 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistor to 5 V.

params.pin: Digital pin the 1-Wire data line is connected to.

begin.summary: Sets or changes the pin of the bus, for an object created without one.

params.pin: Digital pin the 1-Wire data line is connected to.

reset.summary: Sends a reset pulse. Every command starts with a reset.
reset.returns: 1 if at least one device answered, 0 if none.

select.summary: Selects one device by its 8-byte ROM address; the next commands go to it only.

params.rom: 8-byte device address, for example found with search().

skip.summary: Addresses all devices at once (Skip ROM), handy when only one device is connected.

write.summary: Sends one byte on the bus.

params.v: Byte to send, for example a command such as 0x44.
params.power: 1 to keep the line powered afterwards, for parasite-powered devices (default 0).

write_bytes.summary: Sends several bytes on the bus.

params.power: true to keep the line powered afterwards (default false).

read.summary: Reads one byte from the bus.

read_bytes.summary: Reads several bytes from the bus.

depower.summary: Stops powering the line after a write with power set.

search.summary: Finds the next device on the bus. Call it in a loop to list all devices.

params.newAddr: 8-byte array that receives the address found.
params.search_mode: true (default) for a normal search, false to find only devices with an alarm.

search.returns: true if a device was found, false when there are no more.

reset_search.summary: Restarts search() from the first device.

target_search.summary: Makes the next search() look only for one family of devices.

params.family_code: Family code, the first address byte, for example 0x28 for the DS18B20.

crc8.summary: Calculates the 8-bit CRC checksum used to check addresses and data. Call it as OneWire::crc8().

params.len: Number of bytes, for example 7 for an address.

crc8.returns: The CRC; compare it with the byte that follows the data.

crc16.summary: Calculates the 16-bit CRC used by some devices.

check_crc16.summary: Checks data against the inverted 16-bit CRC a device sent.

params.inverted_crc: The 2 CRC bytes received from the device.

print.summary: Sends text or a number as readable characters, without starting a new line.

params.value: Text, a character or a number to print.
params.base: For whole numbers: DEC (default), HEX, OCT or BIN.
params.digits: For decimal numbers: digits after the point (default 2).

println.summary: Like print(), then moves to a new line. With no argument it only ends the line.

params.value: Text, a character or a number to print.
params.base: For whole numbers: DEC (default), HEX, OCT or BIN.
params.digits: For decimal numbers: digits after the point (default 2).

println.returns: Number of characters sent, including the line ending.

write.summary: Sends raw bytes as they are, without turning numbers into text.

params.size: How many bytes of the array to send.

getWriteError.summary: Checks whether an earlier write failed.

clearWriteError.summary: Resets the write error so getWriteError() returns 0 again.

Servo.summary: Creates a servo object. Call attach() in setup() before using it.

attach.summary: Connects the servo to a pin and starts sending pulses.

params.pin: Digital pin the servo signal wire is connected to.
params.min: Pulse width in microseconds for 0 degrees (default 544).
params.max: Pulse width in microseconds for 180 degrees (default 2400).

attach.returns: The channel number used, or 255 if no channel is free.

detach.summary: Stops the pulses and frees the pin.

write.summary: Turns the servo to an angle. Values of 200 or more are taken as a pulse width in microseconds.

writeMicroseconds.summary: Sets the pulse width directly, for finer control than whole degrees.

params.value: Pulse width in microseconds, usually 1000 to 2000.

attached.summary: Checks whether the servo is attached to a pin.

pulseWidth.summary: Shortest, longest and default pulse widths in microseconds (544, 2400, 1500).

MAX_SERVOS.summary: How many servos can be attached at once (12 on the Uno).

SoftwareSerial.summary: Creates a serial port on two digital pins. On the Uno, RX can be any pin with pin-change interrupts (all digital pins).

params.receivePin: Pin that receives data (connect to the module TX).
params.transmitPin: Pin that sends data (connect to the module RX).
params.inverse_logic: true for inverted signals; leave false (default) for normal modules.

begin.summary: Starts the port at a baud rate. Speeds up to 57600 work reliably.

params.speed: Baud rate, for example 9600; must match the module.

end.summary: Stops the port and frees its pins.

listen.summary: Makes this port the one that receives. Only one SoftwareSerial port can receive at a time.
listen.returns: true if another port was listening before.

isListening.summary: Checks whether this port is the one currently receiving.

overflow.summary: Checks whether incoming data was lost because the 64-byte buffer was full. Reading it clears the flag.

SPIClass.summary: The SPI bus class. You do not create it yourself: use the ready-made SPI object.

instance.summary: The SPI bus. Call SPI.begin() in setup() first.

begin.summary: Starts the SPI bus and sets up pins 11, 12 and 13 (and pin 10 as an output).

end.summary: Stops the SPI bus. The pins keep their current mode.

beginTransaction.summary: Claims the bus with the settings your device needs. Pull the chip select pin LOW after this.

params.settings: An SPISettings with clock, bit order and data mode.

endTransaction.summary: Releases the bus so other devices or interrupts can use it.

transfer.summary: Sends data and receives data at the same time. With a buffer, each byte is replaced by the byte received.

params.buf: Array of bytes to send; it is overwritten with the bytes received.
params.count: Number of bytes in the array.

transfer16.summary: Sends and receives a 16-bit value (two bytes) at once.

usingInterrupt.summary: Tells SPI that an interrupt handler also uses the bus, so that interrupt is paused during transactions.

setBitOrder.summary: Old way to set the bit order. Prefer SPISettings with beginTransaction().

setDataMode.summary: Old way to set the data mode. Prefer SPISettings with beginTransaction().

setClockDivider.summary: Old way to set the speed as a fraction of the 16 MHz clock. Prefer SPISettings with beginTransaction().

params.clockDiv: One of SPI_CLOCK_DIV2 to SPI_CLOCK_DIV128 (default SPI_CLOCK_DIV4, 4 MHz).

attachInterrupt.summary: Turns on the SPI interrupt (for advanced peripheral-mode use).

dataMode.summary: SPI data modes 0 to 3: which clock level is idle and on which edge data is read. Check the device datasheet; most use SPI_MODE0.

clockDivider.summary: Divides the 16 MHz clock by 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128 to set the SPI speed (8 MHz down to 125 kHz).

SPISettings.summary: Bundles the speed, bit order and data mode a device needs. Pass it to SPI.beginTransaction(). Without arguments: 4 MHz, MSBFIRST, SPI_MODE0.

params.clock: Highest clock speed the device supports, in hertz (for example 1000000 for 1 MHz).

Stepper.summary: Creates a stepper motor on 2, 4 or 5 control pins.

params.stepsPerRevolution: Steps for one full turn, for example 200 for many motors or 2048 for the 28BYJ-48.

setSpeed.summary: Sets how fast step() turns the motor. It does not start the motor by itself.

step.summary: Turns the motor a number of steps. The sketch waits until the motor has finished.

params.steps: Steps to move; positive for one direction, negative for the other.

available.summary: Checks how many received bytes are waiting to be read.
available.returns: Number of bytes ready (0 if none). The Uno serial buffer holds 64 bytes.

read.summary: Takes the next received byte out of the buffer.
read.returns: The byte (0 to 255), or -1 if nothing is waiting.

peek.summary: Looks at the next received byte without removing it.
peek.returns: The byte (0 to 255), or -1 if nothing is waiting.

setTimeout.summary: Sets how long the waiting functions (parseInt(), readString(), find() …) wait for data.

find.summary: Reads incoming data until a given text is found or the timeout runs out.

params.target: Text (or a single character) to look for.
params.length: How many characters of target to match.

find.returns: true if found, false on timeout.

findUntil.summary: Like find(), but also stops when a terminator text is found.
findUntil.returns: true if target was found, false if the terminator or the timeout came first.

parseInt.summary: Reads the next whole number from incoming text, for example 42 from 42 then Enter. Waits up to the timeout.

params.lookahead: What to skip before the number: SKIP_ALL (default), SKIP_NONE or SKIP_WHITESPACE.
params.ignore: A character to ignore inside the number, such as a comma in 1,000.

parseInt.returns: The number read, or 0 if none came before the timeout.

parseFloat.summary: Reads the next decimal number from incoming text, for example 3.14. Waits up to the timeout.

params.lookahead: What to skip before the number: SKIP_ALL (default), SKIP_NONE or SKIP_WHITESPACE.
params.ignore: A character to ignore inside the number.

parseFloat.returns: The number read, or 0 if none came before the timeout.

readBytes.summary: Reads bytes into an array until it has enough or the timeout runs out.

params.buffer: Array to store the bytes in.
params.length: How many bytes to read at most.

readBytes.returns: Number of bytes actually read (0 if none).

readBytesUntil.summary: Like readBytes(), but also stops at a terminator character, which is not stored.

params.terminator: Character that ends reading, for example a newline.
params.buffer: Array to store the bytes in.
params.length: How many bytes to read at most.

readBytesUntil.returns: Number of bytes stored in buffer.

readString.summary: Reads all incoming characters into a String until nothing new arrives for the timeout.

readStringUntil.summary: Reads incoming characters into a String until a terminator character or the timeout.

params.terminator: Character that ends reading, usually a newline. It is removed from the input but not added to the result.

readStringUntil.returns: The text read, without the terminator.

lookahead.summary: How parseInt() and parseFloat() treat characters before the number: SKIP_ALL skips anything that is not part of a number, SKIP_NONE skips nothing, SKIP_WHITESPACE skips only spaces, tabs and line endings.

String.summary: Creates a text object that can grow and be joined with +. Uses RAM, so avoid very long Strings on the Uno.

params.value: Starting content: text, a character or a number (default empty).
params.base: For whole numbers: number base such as DEC (default) or HEX.
params.decimalPlaces: For decimal numbers: digits after the point (default 2).

length.summary: Counts the characters in the String.

charAt.summary: Gets one character of the String. Same as s[index].
charAt.returns: The character, or 0 if index is past the end.

setCharAt.summary: Replaces one character of the String. Does nothing if index is past the end.

concat.summary: Adds text or a number to the end of the String. Same as +=.

params.value: Text, a character or a number to add.

concat.returns: true on success, false if memory ran out.

compareTo.summary: Compares two Strings in alphabetical (character code) order.
compareTo.returns: A negative number if this comes first, 0 if equal, positive if other comes first.

equals.summary: Checks whether two texts are exactly the same. Same as ==.
equals.returns: true if equal, upper and lower case matter.

equalsIgnoreCase.summary: Checks whether two texts are the same, ignoring upper and lower case.

startsWith.summary: Checks whether the String begins with a given text.
startsWith.returns: true if it starts with prefix.

endsWith.summary: Checks whether the String ends with a given text.
endsWith.returns: true if it ends with suffix.

indexOf.summary: Finds the first place a character or text appears.

params.value: Character or text to look for.

indexOf.returns: Position of the first match, or -1 if not found.

lastIndexOf.summary: Finds the last place a character or text appears, searching backwards.

params.value: Character or text to look for.
params.fromIndex: Position to search backwards from (default the end).

lastIndexOf.returns: Position of the last match, or -1 if not found.

params.from: Position of the first character to copy.
params.to: Position to stop before (default the end).

substring.returns: The part as a new String.

replace.summary: Replaces every occurrence of a character or text with another, changing the String itself.

params.replacement: Character or text to put in its place.

params.index: Position of the first character to delete.
params.count: How many to delete (default all to the end).

toLowerCase.summary: Changes all letters of the String to lowercase.

toUpperCase.summary: Changes all letters of the String to uppercase.

trim.summary: Removes spaces, tabs and line endings from both ends of the String, for example after readStringUntil().

toInt.summary: Converts text such as 123 into a whole number.
toInt.returns: The number, or 0 if the text does not start with a number.

toFloat.summary: Converts text such as 3.14 into a decimal number.
toFloat.returns: The number, or 0 if the text does not start with a number.

toDouble.summary: Converts text into a decimal number (same precision as float on the Uno).
